newsitem.title: USA: U.S. reserving judgment on Iraq food-for-oil deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. reserving judgment on Iraq food-for-oil deal.

text.p: The Clinton administration is reserving judgment on whether Iraq's oil-for-food deal should be continued, Bill Richardson, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, said on Saturday.
"We want to reserve our judgment. We're very concerned with Saddam Hussein's continued violations of the no fly zone," Richardson said on CNN's Evans and Novak program.

Richardson said the Clinton administration has not decided whether to continue the U.N.-brokered deal in which Iraq was allowed to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other essentials for its people.

"We have not made a decision on whether we renew what is called 986, the oil-for-food deal -- the reason being, we want to see some facts on the Iraqi distribution methods, the U.N. implementation of this in northern Iraq," he said.

"...we want to make sure that food is reaching those people, that they are not some oil initiatives there," Richardson said of the deal which went into effect in December is up for renewal next month.
